faq.question: How do I do a full clean rebuild of a Capacitor iOS app?
faq.answer: Rebuild the web app, run bunx cap sync ios, then in Xcode use Product > Clean Build Folder. For SPM projects also use File > Packages > Reset Package Caches. For CocoaPods delete ios/App/Pods and run bunx cap sync ios again. If errors persist, quit Xcode and delete ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData.

faq.question: Which Xcode version do I need for Capacitor 8?
faq.answer: Capacitor 8 requires Xcode 26 or later. Since April 28, 2026, App Store Connect also rejects uploads built with older Xcode versions, so Xcode 26 is required for releases regardless of Capacitor version.

faq.question: How do I see console logs from my Capacitor app on iOS?
faq.answer: Enable the Develop menu in Safari settings, connect the device or start the simulator, then pick the app under Safari > Develop. Debug builds are inspectable by default on iOS 16.4+. For release builds, set ios.webContentsDebuggingEnabled to true in the Capacitor config. Native logs show in the Xcode console.

faq.question: Why do my web changes not appear in the iOS app?
faq.answer: Capacitor copies built web assets into the native project. Run your web build, then bunx cap sync ios or bunx cap copy ios, and run the app again. If you use live updates, the app may also be running a downloaded bundle instead of the built-in one.

faq.question: Should I fix CocoaPods errors or migrate to SPM?
faq.answer: If the error comes from version conflicts or Ruby tooling and all your plugins support SPM, migrating usually removes that whole class of errors. If a plugin you need is CocoaPods-only, fix the CocoaPods issue for now and plan the migration later.
